problem: Navigation frameworks that ground instructions into a single deterministic waypoint or object mask center collapse spatial uncertainty and often target non-traversable locations (e.g. the center of a sofa), causing execution failures. They also cannot express orientation constraints such as 'face the TV'.
motivation: Real-world commands are concise, intent-driven, and refer to targets within the current FOV, unlike turn-by-turn VLN instructions. Bridging semantic identification and physical reachability needs a soft, dense output that a local planner can combine with collision costs and embodiment constraints.
key_idea: Fine-tune Qwen3-VL to predict a navigation-affordance heatmap over reachable floor and a facing heatmap in the egocentric image, and use them as a semantic potential field for an MPPI local planner across robot embodiments.
insight: The feature-fusion ablation shows that decoding directly from VLM features is weak, especially for facing (Facing F1 0.0455), and that re-injecting ViT spatial features via cross-attention with VLM context features gives the best overall F1 (0.6001 vs 0.2592). Replacing VLM features with plain text features in the cross-attention collapses facing (F1 0.0475), so the fusion already formed inside the backbone is valuable. In simulation, the heatmap model roughly doubles SR over the Qwen3-VL baseline on all three robots, while NE is distorted by survivorship bias.
method: Dual-heatmap targets: H_nav is a distance field over traversable pixels (zero on non-traversable pixels, peak at a standable point beside the object); H_fac is a 2D Gaussian at the facing-target mask center; an absent target gives an all-zero map.
Backbone: Qwen3-VL with LoRA (r=16, alpha=32) on attention q/v projections; F_vis comes from three concatenated deepstack ViT levels, and F_vlm from the VLM decoder context projected linearly.
Cross-attention fusion: visual tokens are queries and VLM tokens are keys/values, followed by an FFN residual; a mask hides padding, image and assistant tokens to prevent leakage.

Coordinate-aware decoder: CenterNet-style x,y coordinate channels are concatenated, then a 1x1 bottleneck and ASPP (dilations 1,2,4,8), then two parallel branches of four Resize-Conv upsampling blocks.
Loss: BCE for nav, Gaussian-reweighted focal loss (alpha=2, beta=4) for facing, and dynamic annealing of w_fac toward the end of training.

Synthetic data pipeline: about 130 Isaac Sim scenes (Kujiale, GRUtopia) rendered with RGB, depth and semantics; Gemini normalizes tags and re-renders reference crops; SAM3 gives masks; depth-based 3D distance fields are re-projected to get GT heatmaps; ScanNet, SunRGBD, HyperSim and MP3D are also annotated.
Planner integration: heatmaps are projected to 3D with depth and extrinsics and used as a reward in an MPPI planner, S(tau)=∫(α M_nav + β D_fac)dt, under embodiment-specific kinematics.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL 8B (LoRA fine-tuned) + cross-attention and conv decoder (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Own synthetic Isaac Sim data plus annotated ScanNet, SunRGBD, HyperSim and Matterport3D; 266,766 train and 79,140 test samples (345,906 total)
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (plus depth for heatmap projection to 3D) and interleaved text/image instruction
setting.action_space: dense 2D heatmaps projected to 3D, executed by MPPI local planner trajectories (low-level control per embodiment)
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (ROS2-based) with Jetbot, H1 and Aliengo
setting.privileged: none for the model; depth and camera extrinsics are used for projection; GT is used only for evaluation

numbers_note: Metrics are printed as fractions (0-1) and copied as printed. The benchmark is the authors' own and is not a standard one. Seen-scene results (Jetbot SR 0.7012, H1 0.6004, Aliengo 0.5230) are in Table 3 but not listed as entries. Table 1 says 'MP3D val_test', so the split label is approximate.
results: On the MP3D val_test waypoint benchmark the 8B model reaches Overall F1 0.4917 and Nav R 0.6740, against Qwen3-VL-Instruct at 0.3758 F1 and 0.2044 Nav R, and AR 0.7265 vs 0.2138. In simulation, SR is 0.4790–0.6517 on unseen scenes across Jetbot, H1 and Aliengo, versus 0.1548–0.3686 for the fine-tuned Qwen3-VL point baseline.
limitations: Evaluation is simulation-only with no real-robot experiments, and the benchmark is self-built with metrics not comparable to standard VLN/ObjectNav. The baselines are zero-shot models, while the proposed model is trained on the authors' data, so the comparison is not like-for-like.
Restricted to in-FOV targets, with no long-horizon exploration or memory, and NE results are confounded by survivorship bias. Nav precision remains low (0.30).
The planner-level ablation of heatmaps vs point waypoints is only qualitative or against a single baseline; the α, β weights and MPPI details are unspecified.
